newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up in active trading on Monday with institutions borrowing money to trade new shares on Shanghai's domestic A share market, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract rose to 11.70 percent from 11.51 percent last Friday.
Turnover surged to 9.08 million lots from 5.12 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said new A shares attracted much liquidity from the repo market. Ningbo Huatong was listed today and China Liaoning International Cooperation (Group) will issues share tomorrow.
"Most of the rates were pushed up due to heavy borrowing for speculation on the A share market," one trader said. "The rates are likely to continue to be firm in the short term."

Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down on Monday on profit-taking after a short-lived technical rebound last Friday, traders said. The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 dropped to 122.28 yuan from 122.85.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market plunged to 587,181 lots from 1.10 million lots.
Traders expect the contracts to consolidate at low levels in the short term due to weak sentiment after months of falls.
